digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure - ACLI subprocess timeouts and snapshot fetch stalls
propositions: Five ACLI subprocess reap tests each waste ~1s waiting for a blanket 1s timeout fixture to fire, despite asserting on child-side setup that must complete before the deadline.

A sixth ACLI test (read-retry with rate-limit backoff) inherits the 1s blanket timeout as an implicit pass condition, creating a latent load flake where two spawned children must complete within that ceiling.

Three reap tests assert on child-side artifacts (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, flushed partial stdout) whose ordering depends only on the injected window being larger than interpreter startup, not on explicit synchronization.
The snapshot stall abort test injects a 2s low-speed window although its sibling dribble test already proves git honors a 1s window, wasting ~1s per run.

Replacing blanket timeout with opt-in fixtures and explicit readiness gates (file polling before returning process to parent) removes wall-clock races and enables shrinking real-time windows from 1–2s to 0.1–1s without flakiness.
